title: Replica Merges Stale Local Edits at Apply
description: Root fix: when the replica applies an inbound event on a path holding an unpublished local edit made on a stale view (written >30 s after the event), it moves the local bytes to .cache/f/lost and agents lose live work during catch-up (g1-m05 2026-11-23: NativeReceive derive edits lost 3x). Instead, merge three-way at apply time: base = the replica's known (last applied) version from the blob store, ours = local file, theirs = inbound. A clean merge is written and published by the normal publish path; only a real conflict keeps the inbound and moves the local bytes to lost. Own diff3 implementation (no runtime deps), schema-first, language-agnostic test vectors validated against git merge-file.
summary: The replica apply now three-way merges a losing local edit with the inbound put. The base is the content it last applied at the path, read from its blob and sha-verified; the new module is 🔁️replica/🔀️merge (mergeTextV1, no dependencies). A clean merge is written over the fleet content (event `merged`) and publishes as a local edit once caught up. Conflicts, binary files, sides over 8 MiB or 4096 line edits, and a missing base keep the old rule: fleet content stays, local bytes go to lost, `stale-base` (now emitted after the install). Schema-first vectors: all 18 agree with git merge-file, plus 300 seeded random cases where every clean merge equals git. The replica scenario fixture gained a merge scenario (passes on Windows). A POSIX fleet test was added but not run here (no Linux bun). The README documents rule (3). The live daemon on g1-m05 runs the new code. Report: replica-apply-merge.md.
